srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in 1997, this album is considered The Prodigy's masterpiece, one of the best electronic music albums ever, and one of the most relevant albums of the 1990s. With this record, The Prodigy took a significant leap forward, creating much more complex music. A crucial factor was Keith Flint's creative involvement; previously a mere figurehead, he contributed to the album's creative process, introducing a much more violent, punk and rock-influenced sound, with heavily distorted guitars and even some ska elements. This brought a very interesting renewal to The Prodigy's sound and a step forward in the iconography of their music videos. It became the quintessential "electronic punk album" and the album of an entire angry generation, selling millions worldwide despite many radio stations refusing to play it and its music videos being censored. "The Fat of the Land is the electronic punk album par excellence and it was the album of a generation."

srcs.episode: The Prodigy: Electrónica y rabia que hizo historia

podcast.body: Released in 1997, this album is considered the most important for the expansion of the Big Beat genre and arguably the most beloved and remembered by the public. It sold approximately 10 million copies worldwide and was not the band's debut, but their third studio work. Although The Prodigy had previously been rooted in the hardcore rave scene, their transition to Big Beat allowed them to maintain a rebellious, hip-hop-like attitude. "Fatof de L'Ans Laura Maestra del genero y el principal causante de su éxito. Vendió alrededor de 10 millones de copias en todo el mundo."
